Enforced by scripts/ci/check_lever_reachability.py: the registry `arm_r` must equal config/strategies.yaml, so changing an arm without re-measuring FAILS CI. Design: docs/design/position-telemetry-DESIGN.md. Finding: BL-20260816-TRAIL-DECAY-ARM-R-SITS-ABOVE-THE-VENUE-TP-CAP (PR #9588). THIS FILE RECORDS MEASUREMENTS AND DISPOSITIONS — it changes no behaviour and no value; every arm_r correction is Tier-3 and the operator's.

basis_note: `order_packages/risk_per_unit` is the AUTHORITATIVE basis — the sized risk the strategy actually used. `entry - stop_loss` is NOT the entry risk (a stop is trailed and amended, and the error has no fixed sign: measured 2026-08-16 the two agreed at 1.00 on gld/qqq, 0.71 on xrp, and 5.66x on one trend_donchian package). `candles/atr` is a cheap unconditional screen and is NOT a bound in either direction — on xrp it overstated reachability 90.5% vs 33.3% because entries are filter-selected. | ⚠️ **THE OPERATIVE CEILING IS THE VENUE TP CAP — `0.099/(risk_per_unit/entry)`, which is what `order_packages.tp` ENCODES AND WHAT THE BROKER IS SENT.** Verified in code 2026-08-16, not inferred from a field: `src/units/accounts/execute.py:391` builds the order with `"tp": pkg.tp`; `:703` and `:1467` send `kwargs["takeProfit"] = quantize_price(order["tp"], tick)`; `:1875`/`:1912` journal `take_profit_1 = float(pkg.tp)`. That TP fills and ends the trade, so it bounds the MFE a lever could ever see. ⚠️ **DO NOT read `exit_plan_state.targets[].reach_r` as the ceiling.** It is `min(venue_cap_R, DEFAULT_MAX_REACH_R=5.0)` from the **OBSERVE-ONLY** ExitPlan ladder (`src/runtime/exit_plan_realism.py:44` + `exit_plan_materializer`), which is recorded and **never placed**: the only exit-plan reference in `execute.py` is the soak block at `:630-648`, whose own comment says *"nothing reads it back (graduation to a real laddered exit is the backtest-gated P4)"*, and `exit_plan_state` appears nowhere else in `src/` except the materializer and DB serialization. Reading it **UNDER**-reports the ceiling and manufactures false `inert` verdicts. Worked example: `pkg-61cb138b930c4a05` carries `tp = 117.66993` (entry 107.07, +9.90% = the venue cap, **7.19R** — PLACED) beside `exit_plan_state.targets[0].price = 114.445` (**5.0R** — counterfactual). `realism_notes[].reach_r` holds the PRE-clamp value and therefore agrees with the identity; it is not a trap. **BLAST RADIUS if the clamped field is used:** it caps every observation at 5.0, so the three arms ABOVE the clamp — `trend_donchian` 6.49, `trend_donchian_sol_4h` 5.57, `gld_pullback_1d` 5.06 — would grade a blanket false `inert` (`trend_donchian` flips from reachable-at-100% to inert). Arms BELOW 5.0 are unaffected, because `min(x,5) >= arm` iff `x >= arm` when `arm < 5` — which is why `xrp_pullback_2h`'s 2/37 count (arm 4.49) is correct as recorded. ⚠️ **TWO PRIOR REVISIONS OF THIS NOTE WERE WRONG IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS**, recorded so neither is re-derived: one said the identity was authoritative for the wrong reason (that `reach_r` under-reports *because* it is not cap_R), and its retraction said `targets[].reach_r` was the operative ceiling. The settled test is neither 'which field looks authoritative' nor 'which is more conservative' — it is **which value reaches `kwargs["takeProfit"]`**, which is a code path and is the evidence cited above. See PB-20260816-REACH-R-IS-CLAMPED-NOT-CAP-R.

evidence_flag_policy._what: Is a reach-share verdict SETTLED, or a point estimate over a sample too small to grade? Computed by scripts/ops/lever_evidence_flag.py from each basis's k and n; NEVER hand-written. The guard `lever-evidence-flag-guard` fails when a stored share, interval or flag does not reproduce from its own k/n under this policy.
evidence_flag_policy.method_why: Exact (inverted binomial test), so coverage is >= nominal at EVERY n rather than on average, and it is conservative -- wider than Wilson. For a flag whose job is refusing to overclaim, erring wide errs in the right direction. [!] THE DISPATCH PROPOSED WILSON AND THIS DELIBERATELY DEPARTS FROM IT, with a measured reason: 95% Wilson puts the lower bound on 1 of 1 at 20.6%, which clears the 10% settled_reachable cut-point -- a flag built to stop a verdict overclaiming its denominator would have declared a SINGLE observation settled, and trend_donchian's only entry-conditioned basis is exactly n=1. Clopper-Pearson gives 2.5% for that cell, i.e. unsettled. Over the nine cells the dispatch tabulated with Wilson the two methods assign the SAME flag to every one, so the swap changes no published verdict; it changes the one cell the table did not include.
evidence_flag_policy.status: UNDERIVED -- NO CUT-POINT HAS BEEN DERIVED, AND THE TWO THAT WERE PROPOSED ARE WITHDRAWN. A first version of this block carried settled_inert_ci_high_below_pct: 2.0 and settled_reachable_ci_low_at_or_above_pct: 10.0. The operator REJECTED both on 2026-09-22, verbatim: "we need data-backed values, not arbitrary ones (otherwise what's the point of the arm in the first place?)" -- and was right: a threshold picked to make a table come out is the same species of unearned number as the p80 arms this registry exists to audit. The two fields are DELETED rather than set to null, so nothing can read them as adopted-but-empty. What replaces them is `plausible_cut_band` below, which asserts strictly less. Deriving a real cut-point is OPEN WORK, specified on checklist row E41 and not done here.

vocabulary.settled_inert: the interval's UPPER bound is below settled_inert_ci_high_below_pct -- we looked, over enough entries, and the arm is dead
vocabulary.settled_reachable: the interval's LOWER bound is at or above settled_reachable_ci_low_at_or_above_pct -- we looked and the arm fires
vocabulary.unsettled: neither -- WE LOOKED AND CANNOT TELL. The interval spans both cut-points.
vocabulary.not_measured: n == 0 -- WE COULD NOT LOOK. Distinct from `unsettled` in the direction that matters.

evidence_flag_policy.three_states_never_collapsed: `unsettled` is NOT `unmeasured` and NOT `inert`, and this is the whole point of the flag: today an `inert` on n=8 and an `inert` on n=127 are the same word. `unmeasured`/`not_measured` says we could not look; `settled_inert` says we looked and it is dead; `unsettled` says we looked and cannot tell. Collapsing the third into either is the class docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md section 'Collapsed states' and scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py exist for. The script's --self-test carries a NON-VACUITY CONTROL -- a cell that MUST come out `unsettled` -- so a flag that had quietly lost its ability to say 'I don't know' would fail rather than look clean.
evidence_flag_policy.primary_basis_rule: The entry-level flag is taken from ONE basis, chosen by a declared rule rather than by whichever reads best: a basis on the CURRENT geometry beats a stale one; then live_entry_conditioned beats backtest_entry_conditioned; then larger n. A `candle_screen` is NEVER primary -- this file's own basis_note records the screen overstating reachability 90.5% vs 33.3% on xrp because entries are filter-selected.
evidence_flag_policy.geometry_field: `current` / `stale` / `unknown`, never collapsed. cap_R = 0.099/(atr_stop_mult*ATR/entry) and the operative ceiling is min(cap_R, tp_r), so a measurement stops describing its leg the moment either knob moves -- which is exactly what happened to trend_donchian_sol_4h (atr_stop_mult 2.5 -> 1.5) and scha_trend_long_1d (tp_r 50.0 -> 1.5) after 2026-08-16. `unknown` means nobody has checked whether the knobs moved; it is NOT `current`.

plausible_cut_band._what: The band of cut-points still OPEN. A `settled_*` flag is emitted only where the verdict is INVARIANT across this whole band -- i.e. it holds for EVERY cut-point nobody has ruled out -- rather than for one somebody picked. That is why this file can say anything at all while the cut-point is underived: it states only what survives not knowing it.

Any reachable cut-point that would grade that lever NOT reachable is refuted by the firing itself, so the band cannot extend above the lower bound of its interval, 88.4%. plausible_cut_band.inert_cut_anchor: [!] THERE IS NO ANCHOR ON THE INERT SIDE, AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS DELIBERATE: with `inert_cut_lower_pct` null, `settled_inert` IS UNREACHABLE -- no entry in this file can currently be graded a settled dead arm, whatever its numbers.
